Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Acme POC

Hi Olivia / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned for the trial/POC: 

Recap
- Goal: validate an on-prem/dedicated trial of Redwood inference to power Acme's customer support assistant for EN/ES/FR. Primary focus: intent classification + concise answer generation from internal KB.
- Success criteria (from call): 
  - Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on Acme's evaluation set (weighted by traffic)
  - Typical response latency (95th percentile) <= 350ms for single-turn queries on Dedicated capacity
  - No PII leakage across calls; logs retained per Acme retention policy (30d)

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Redwood to propose a trial model & fallback pair and a config for Dedicated trial (batching, KV cache, quantization). Dev to propose by EOD Monday.
2) Acme to share a representative evaluation set (CSV) and confirm languages and traffic mix.
3) Agree on timeline & ownership below.

Timeline / owners (proposed)
- Tue (3/2): Acme shares eval set + success criteria spreadsheet (Olivia / Samir)
- Wed (3/3): Redwood provides model selection, trial config, and preliminary cost estimate (Dev Patel)
- Thu-Fri (3/4-3/5): Redwood spins up Dedicated trial and runs initial smoke tests (Marissa / Dev)
- Week of 3/8: Joint evaluation & iterative tuning; decision by 3/12

Attachments: I attached a suggested success_criteria template and a sample trial_config.

Please reply with any additions or confirm and we’ll proceed.

Thanks,
Aditya

Thanks, Aditya — helpful recap.

A few clarifications / asks from our side: 
- We can share the eval set by end of day Tuesday (3/2). The initial set will be ~2k anonymized tickets (EN 70%, ES 20%, FR 10%).

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Acme POC

Hi Olivia — thanks, and great to see the language mix. Below is a pragmatic model selection and trial plan that aligns with Acme's priorities (quality for EN/ES/FR, predictable latency on Dedicated, and cost-aware fallback):

Model selection (recommended)
- Primary model (quality / multilingual): Llama-2-13b-chat (open weights) — strong multilingual capabilities with chat tuning; we recommend the 13b chat variant as the sweet spot for quality/latency on your traffic mix.
- Fallback model (lower-cost / high-throughput): Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized 4-bit) — lower token cost and good performance for shorter generations and classification tasks.
- Quantization & runtime: we'll run both models quantized to 4-bit where supported on Dedicated to reduce memory and cost; for Llama-2-13b-chat we recommend GPTQ/4-bit + KV-cache warmup to hit your 95p latency target.

Evaluation plan & metrics
- Datasets: use Acme's 2k anonymized tickets split EN/ES/FR. Redwood will also generate a synthetic adversarial subset (~200 examples) to test edge cases and PII leakage.
- Metrics to report: top-1 intent accuracy, intent confusion matrix, slot F1, answer relevance (human eval sample), token cost per 1k queries, 95th latency (ms), memory utilization.
- Acceptance criteria (proposal):
  - Intent top-1 accuracy >= 94% (we can tune prompts and few-shot examples if needed)
  - Slot F1 >= 0.86
  - 95p latency <= 350ms on Dedicated baseline (with configured batching and KV cache)
  - PII redaction: zero incidents in synthetic PII tests; integration with AWS KMS for keying

Trial config & timeline
- Wed 3/3 (today): Redwood to produce trial config (attached redwood_trial_config.yaml) and cost estimate for 2-week Dedicated run.
- Thu 3/4: Spin up Dedicated trial capacity (dev + infra) and baseline smoke tests using a 200-sample subset.
- Week 3/8-3/12: Run full evaluation set, iterate on prompts, and produce final report by 3/12.

Ownership
- Acme: Olivia + Samir — provide eval set, accept report, and run human eval for relevance samples.
- Redwood: Dev Patel (technical lead) — trial execution, baseline tuning, and report; Marissa Cole (ops) — provisioning + monitoring; Aditya — commercial and coordination.

Next steps (today)
1) Olivia to share eval CSV and filled success criteria spreadsheet.
2) Redwood will confirm Dedicated instance sizes and provide a cost estimate by EOD.
3) We'll schedule a Tuesday 3/9 sync to review results (tentative).

Notes on multilingual tuning
- For ES/FR, we'll include language-specific few-shot exemplars in the prompt set and, if needed, a lightweight translation-fallback path: run English model + machine-translate for short answers only if native output underperforms. We'll flag this in the report if observed.

Security & KMS
- We support AWS KMS integration for key wrapping of logs; we'll provide an audit of log retention and redaction options as part of the trial docs.

Attachments referenced: redwood_trial_config.yaml (config with instance sizes/batching settings) and a template acceptance spreadsheet.

Let me know if you'd like the primary model to be a Llama-2-70b-chat instead — that would raise quality for complex generation but requires larger Dedicated capacity and will increase cost.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
